rows.50:9e6c:
There was a fire extinguisher in the corner of the hallway.
The instant I caught sight of it, {f:I|I} lost all sense of what I was doing.{p}
rows.50:9f04:
......When I came to my senses, {f:I|I} was clutching a bloodstained fire extinguisher.
Arai lay in front of me, drenched in blood.
He had to be dead for real this time.
As {f:I|I} stood there in a daze, thinking just that, Kazama rounded on me.
"What were you thinking?! He'd finally come back to life!
You're the one who killed him, you hear me?!"
Before Kazama could finish, a voice called from down the hallway.
"What are you doing there★"
It was the teacher on night duty.
Kazama shouted at the top of his lungs, as if he'd forgotten whose side he'd been on a moment ago.
"It's terrible! Please, come quickly☆"
...{f:I|I} had become a murderer.
I couldn't even bring myself to resent Kazama.
Nothing mattered anymore...{p}{f:I|I} didn't even try to run. I just watched the teacher hurrying toward me.{p}
rows.50:a198:
{f:I|I} pressed my ear to Arai's chest.
There was a wheezing sound.
Had he really come back to life {f:after all|after all}?
The very next moment, I realized that was impossible.
When we'd checked earlier, Arai had definitely been dead.
And then there was this sound.
If it were breathing, it couldn't be coming from inside his chest{f:!|!}
What on earth {f:was|was} this sound★
{f:We|We} looked at each other.
The thing lying there no longer seemed like Arai. It seemed like something far more evil.
I had to run.
I had to get away from this place.{p}
rows.50:a47c:
Fighting back nausea, {f:I|I} lifted the arm.
We took turns carrying him. How long did it take us to reach the incinerator?{p}
rows.50:a6fc:
Kazama was trying to shut the incinerator door.
But the hinges were stiff and it wouldn't close.
"Tch, what's wrong with this thing..."
Muttering, he leaned in to look. And at that moment...{p}
rows.50:ab9c:
Kazama's burns weren't serious.
If we kept quiet, Arai would {f:probably just|just} be listed as missing.
...There {f:was|was} no other way.
{f:We|We} left the school without a word.
Tomorrow, the day after, and every day after that, {f:we|we} would surely keep our silence.
{f:We|We} knew that silence was the only way to protect ourselves.
......That should have been the end of it.
But.
Something {f:happened|happened} that wouldn't let it end.
Arai is angry with {f:me|me}.
I wondered why it was {f:me|me} and not Kazama...
I'm sure Arai {f:believed|had believed} that {f:I|I} was on his side.
That's why he's angry that {f:I|I} helped Kazama{f:.|.}
Maybe he feels betrayed.
In his anger, Arai......latched onto {f:me|me}.
Day and night, he clings to {f:me|me} and won't leave.
To people who don't believe in ghosts, he {f:probably seems|must seem} like nothing but a hallucination born of my guilt over him.
But that's not what he is.
{f:I|I} know... only {f:I|I} know.
No, anyone with even a little sixth sense {f:should|should} be able to see him.
After all, even now he's right here beside me.{p}
rows.50:b33c:
It was Kazama{f:!|!}
The burns had changed his face.
His hate-filled eyes glared at {f:me|me}.
You're coming with me.
I thought I heard a voice say it.
Where he gripped my arm, there rose the sickening smell of sizzling flesh.
Bug after bug, turned to fireballs, slammed into me and set my {f:shirt|uniform} alight.
The roar of flames swirling around my ears drowned out everything.
{f:I|I} was engulfed in flames.{p}
rows.50:bea8:
"Everyone, do you understand now?
Spirits are not merely something you feel. They truly exist."
No one said a word.
"If a few more spirits had gathered, even I would not have been able to drive them away."
Arai went on.
Kazama wore a serious expression.
{f:I think he was|He was probably} considering what to make of what he'd just seen.
"Now, I will begin my story.
It is the story of how I came to master this power."{p}
rows.50:c0e4:
Outside the window floated a blue spirit like the ones Arai had shown us earlier.
But it was far bigger than the ones in the room had been. There was no comparison.
Arai was staring out the window, his face full of fear.
"Th-this has turned into a catastrophe..."
His eyes dropped to the floor as he murmured.
A tremendous wind was raging through the room.
"I-it's hopeless..."
With that murmur, Arai began to shake violently.
"Arai! Isn't there anything you can do?"
{f:I|I} called out to him.
But there was no trace left of his earlier composure.
His face was pale, and his eyes wouldn't focus.
Maybe he sensed how bad this was even more than {f:we|we} did.
The girls screamed.
Just like before, the room was filling with that thick, oozing stuff.
Everyone {f:seemed|seemed} to be writhing, trying to peel off the foreign matter sticking to their bodies.
The spirit floating outside the window {f:seemed|seemed} to be growing steadily bigger.
The wind raging through the room looked as if it had started to glow pale blue.
This might be the end.
{f:I|I} had a feeling it was.
How {f:did|did} it come to this?
Maybe the seven wonders of the school were something {f:we|we} should never have touched as a half-joking project.
If only I hadn't taken on this article.....
Regret whirled through my head.
Everyone else {f:looked|looked} completely lost, too.
In the middle of it all, Kazama suddenly spoke up.{p}
rows.50:db14:
"{a}{f:|}, Kazama didn't do as {f:I|I} told him.
He opened his eyes earlier.
He can't talk about it, and besides, you're better off not knowing."
Arai fixed his gaze on Kazama.
"He took this matter far too lightly."
Arai said it flatly.
"{a}{f:|}, there are things in this world better left unknown."
"What do you mean?"
"{a}{f:|}, it seems you're one of those worthless people too.
...If you insist that much, I'll show you what he saw.
It would be cruel to drag the others into it.
Why don't we go to a classroom nearby?"{p}
rows.50:dd5c:
Arai got up from his seat and went out into the hallway.
{f:I|I} followed after him.
A wave of unease washed over me.
What {f:was|was} going to happen now?
{f:I|I} was starting to regret this.
{f:Wasn't I|Wasn't I} walking into something terrible, all because of some petty sense of justice?
That whiff of danger {f:I|I} had instinctively sensed from Arai back then.
Why {f:hadn't|hadn't} I trusted that feeling?
Petty common sense had gotten in the way, and I'd failed to heed the danger signal my instincts had picked up.
Arai went into a nearby classroom.
Holding back the urge to run, {f:I|I} got ready to follow him.
But I could feel some part of me warning me to run.{p}
rows.50:e004:
And so I followed Arai into the classroom.
To the very end, I couldn't heed the warning my instincts gave me.{p}
